quality_snapshot.text:
The air was thick with the scent of damp earth and decaying leaves as Jenna pushed through the underbrush, her heart pounding with the rhythm of her footsteps. Each crack of a twig beneath her worn boots sent a jolt of adrenaline coursing through her veins, a reminder that she was not alone in this tangled expanse of trees and shadows. She paused, her breath hitching in her throat, listening. The distant sound of a brook bubbling over smooth stones mingled with the rustle of unseen creatures scurrying through the brush.

“Are you sure this is the right way?” Mark’s voice broke through the stillness, tinged with a nervous edge. He was a few paces behind her, the crunch of his footsteps just soft enough to be swallowed by the surrounding wilderness.

Jenna turned slightly, her brow furrowed. “We’ve come this far,” she replied, forcing a confidence she didn’t entirely feel. The map had been a tattered mess, the ink smeared and fading, but the promise of the hidden glen had been too tempting to resist. “It has to be around here somewhere.”

The sun dipped lower, casting long, spindly shadows across the forest floor. Flecks of light danced through the leaves overhead, illuminating motes of dust that hung in the air—a fleeting glimpse of magic, or perhaps just a trick of the fading light. She could almost hear the laughter of childhood ghosts, echoing in the spaces between the trees, urging her forward.

Mark sighed, the sound heavy with skepticism. “I just hope we don’t end up lost. I can’t face another night in these woods.” He shifted his weight, his anxiety palpable.

She could feel his unease gnawing at her, a tension that prickled against her skin. The thought of turning back scraped against her resolve, igniting a flicker of defiance within.

The map had been a faded relic, the ink blurred and barely legible, yet the allure of the hidden glen had beckoned her deeper into the woods. “It has to be around here somewhere.”
